root_cause_criterion.criterion: When on_mesh_prefix_was_removed selects the NCP-origin SLAAC address for removal, the source-level object later passed into unicast_address_was_removed() must be a by-value copy rather than a reference alias to addr_iter->first, so erasing mUnicastAddresses cannot invalidate it before TunnelIPv6Interface::remove_address() reads it.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original binds `address` as `const struct in6_addr &address = addr_iter->first;`, so `&address` aliases the map-key storage owned by the `mUnicastAddresses` node. The fixed original changes this to `struct in6_addr address = addr_iter->first;`, preserving the address bytes after the map node is erased.

nodes.state: `remove_address()` dereferences the forwarded `addr` pointer in `IN6_IS_ADDR_UNSPECIFIED(addr)`, which is the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-use-after-free read.
`mUnicastAddresses.erase(address)` is the free site that deletes the map node whose key storage is aliased by the root-cause `address` object.

edges.relation: The same `address` object selected at the root-cause site is the key object passed into `mUnicastAddresses.erase(address)`.
After `mUnicastAddresses.erase(address)` frees the aliased map node, the same `&address` object is immediately reused as the pointer argument to `mPrimaryInterface->remove_address(&address, ...)`.
The dangling pointer passed as `&address` in unicast_address_was_removed() becomes the `addr` argument dereferenced by TunnelIPv6Interface::remove_address().
